ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee; no refund to be issued. Advise the rider via RydeHELP that the driver's arrival was confirmed by GPS within the 200 m pickup radius and that a wait of more than 3 minutes was recorded before cancellation.
ruling.reasoning:
The case enters the NS group because the cancellation was made by the driver while asserting the rider no-showed, so it is assessed under NS-0 → NS-1 [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The $6.61 fee is the standard cancellation fee on record, so the only question is whether NS-1 (i)–(iii) all hold [F7][NS-1].

On (i) and (ii): the record shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 and the GPS placed him 178 m from the pickup point at that exact moment — inside the 200 m radius [F6]. The tap is recorded as a driver action, and the driver's own chat message at 14:06 corroborates that he had arrived at the side road [F9][F6][NS-1].

On (iii): the trace shows the driver remained continuously inside the 200 m radius for 220 s after the 14:06:15 tap, until he cancelled at 14:09:55; 220 s exceeds the 180 s (more than 3 minutes) threshold, and the samples run from the arrival confirmation through to the cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold [F2][F4][F6][NS-1]. The driver's stationary interval of 4 min 0 s at 179 m from the pickup covers the same window [F3]. The requirement of continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes is therefore met.

The rider's complaint is that the driver was not at the entrance where the pin was [F10]. That is a statement of where the rider expected the car, and it conflicts with the system records of position; system records (gps / timeline) control over statements, and 178–179 m is inside the 200 m arrival radius used for NS-1 (ii) [F3][F6][F10][NS-1]. The chat history is complete — 3 messages, all timestamped, none suggesting any threat or refusal to wait — so nothing displaces the timeline [F12][F11][NS-1].

Because all three NS-1 elements pass, the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid and is retained; the driver's wait and cancellation follow the published no-show procedure, so no refund arises and no account action is called for. The safety screen finds no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, the rider's complaint or the driver's statement; it is a plain pickup-location dispute [F9][F10][F11][F13]. The record settles every element the ruling needs, so evidence is sufficient and no escalation is required [F2][F4][F6][F12][NS-1].
